vm.configurationYaml:
minimumLimaVersion: 2.2.1
base: []
vmType: vz
arch: aarch64
cpus: 4
memory: 9GiB
disk: 48GiB
images:
- location: "/Users/ryuman/tmp-mcicon-f2/inputs/base.img"
  arch: aarch64
  digest: sha256:1d6bffe64b848468ac97f821d369a4846d983de1800ccf6b5ec8853e85cefc55
vmOpts:
  vz:
    rosetta:
      enabled: true
      binfmt: true
mountType: virtiofs
mounts:
- location: "/Users/ryuman/tmp-mcicon-f2/package-1/image/MCIconHelper.app/Contents/app/support/offline"
  mountPoint: /mcicon/offline
  writable: false
- location: /Users/ryuman/tmp-mcicon-f2/repo
  mountPoint: /Users/ryuman/tmp-mcicon-f2/repo
  writable: false
- location: /Users/ryuman/tmp-mcicon-f2/run
  mountPoint: /Users/ryuman/tmp-mcicon-f2/run
  writable: true
containerd:
  system: false
  user: false
ssh:
  loadDotSSHPubKeys: false
  forwardAgent: false
  forwardX11: false
propagateProxyEnv: false
upgradePackages: false
provision:
- mode: dependency
  skipDefaultDependencyResolution: true
  script: |
    #!/bin/sh
    exit 0
- mode: system
  script: |
    #!/bin/sh
    set -eu
    export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
    dpkg -i /mcicon/offline/debs/runc.deb /mcicon/offline/debs/containerd.deb /mcicon/offline/debs/docker.io.deb
    usermod -aG docker ryuman
    systemctl enable --now containerd docker
    dpkg-query -W runc containerd docker.io > /var/tmp/mcicon-f2-packages
    systemctl is-active containerd docker > /var/tmp/mcicon-f2-daemons

native.stdout:
Lima: Linux virtual machines

Usage:
  limactl [command]

Examples:
  Start the default instance:
  $ limactl start

  Open a shell:
  $ lima

  Run a container:
  $ lima nerdctl run -d --name nginx -p 8080:80 nginx:alpine

  Stop the default instance:
  $ limactl stop

  See also template YAMLs: /Users/ryuman/tmp-mcicon-f2/package-1/image/MCIconHelper.app/Contents/app/support/share/lima/templates

Basic Commands:
  create              Create an instance of Lima
  delete              Delete an instance of Lima
  edit                Edit an instance of Lima or a template
  list                List instances of Lima
  restart             Restart a running instance
  shell               Execute shell in Lima
  start               Start an instance of Lima
  stop                Stop an instance

Advanced Commands:
  autostart           Manage automatic startup of Lima instances
  clone               Clone an instance of Lima
  copy                Copy files between host and guest
  disk                Lima disk management
  factory-reset       Factory reset an instance of Lima
  info                Show diagnostic information
  network             Lima network management
  protect             Protect an instance to prohibit accidental removal
  prune               Prune garbage objects
  rename              Rename an instance of Lima
  screenshot          Capture a screenshot of the VM display
  show-ssh            Show the SSH command line (DEPRECATED; use `ssh -F` instead)
  snapshot            Manage instance snapshots
  sudoers             Generate the content of the /etc/sudoers.d/lima file
  template            Lima template management (EXPERIMENTAL)
  tunnel              Create a tunnel for Lima
  unprotect           Unprotect an instance
  validate            Validate YAML templates
  watch               Watch events from instances

Available Plugins (Experimental):

Additional Commands:
  completion          Generate the autocompletion script for the specified shell
  help                Help about any command

Flags:
      --debug               Debug mode
  -h, --help                help for limactl
      --log-format string   Set the logging format [text, json] (default "text")
      --log-level string    Set the logging level [trace, debug, info, warn, error]
      --tty                 Enable TUI interactions such as opening an editor. Defaults to true when stdout is a terminal. Set to false for automation.
  -v, --version             version for limactl
  -y, --yes                 Alias of --tty=false

Additional help topics:
  limactl yq-restrictions     Restrictions on yq expressions in Lima

Use "limactl [command] --help" for more information about a command.
